scope: One native trust-recording, ordinary relaunch, human-question callback and durable-history baseline on each platform
review: Sol prepared; Root and independent Astra rejected V1 cleanup/history gaps, reviewed V2 and source-derived V3 prompt oracle; Root ran and checked both platform receipts; Astra independently audited Mac native history and approved unchanged Linux scope.
behavior: Fresh private home and synthetic workspace start without a copied trust entry. Native initialize records the authorized fixture trust choice; a new ordinary process then loads project features.

Direct native stream-JSON retains normal settings, native default prompt and tools. User/project/local instruction canaries, model/effort precedence, a deny rule and a project SessionStart hook remain effective.
One original UUID-bearing user task produces one real native AskUserQuestion request. The host returns its authorized fixture answer against the actual request ID.
Native history after exit has explicitly session-bound, ordered original user, exact tool call, successful result and final answer; the stored tool-result digest equals the subsequent native request.
containment: Only fake credentials and a nonforwarding loopback server; generated private homes; bounded streams, requests and artifacts; exact owned process groups and joined HTTP readers. Linux additionally used a private verified executable copy, Python 3.11.11, an inner 55-second SIGTERM deadline and a hard 60-second whole-cgroup limit with zero stop grace. No live accounts or discussions.

prior_outcomes.v1: Not executed: review found TLS cleanup import, post-spawn ownership, failure-receipt and unordered history-oracle defects.

v2.reason: The test expected the interactive CLI identity line. Pinned source and private native request shapes establish a distinct noninteractive identity with the default native prompt builder.

prior_outcomes.v3: Fresh runs use a source-derived conjunction of identity, native role, harness, permission and action-authorization sections. Minimal/custom/missing-section controls reject. Other behavioral and history checks are unchanged.

limits: This proves basic local structured operation, not terminal UI equivalence or complete workflow parity.
Quota continuation, completed answers, pending approvals/questions across restart, cancellation, queued user input, background tasks, hooks, MCP and workflows remain separate gates.
The fixture supplied explicit synthetic trust and question choices; no production automatic approval policy is implied.
No SDK dependency, product frontend, default mode or live deployment changed.
